trust_decision.summary: Whether a dependent-volume definition inside an imported instance backup is usable is decided in the storage backend at internal/server/storage/backend.go:9480-9524; at the pinned commit it decides by dereferencing disk.Volume, disk.Pool and each volume-snapshot entry, so an index whose dependent_volumes entry omits volume/pool (or has a null snapshot element) panics instead of returning a bad-definition error.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names instance backup import and an omitted volume, and this is the only loop over srcBackup.Config.DependentVolumes; the dereferences of disk.Volume/disk.Pool and snap.Name are in the same few lines.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /1.0/instances with a backup file (cmd/incusd/instances_post.go:845,986) -> storage.CreateInstanceFromBackup -> createDependentVolumesFromBackup; client wrapper is CLI `incus import` (cmd/incus/import.go:94)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can dismiss the migration twin because the advisory names backup-file import: createDependentVolumesFromMigration is reached over the instance-migration transport from a peer Incus server and never touches an uploaded backup archive, so its unguarded dereferences look like a different feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate dependent-volume entry may carry a nil/empty volume_snapshots slice and nil unrelated sub-configs (container, bucket, profiles, snapshots); only a nil Volume/Pool or a nil snapshot element is invalid. A blanket 'reject any nil field' guard, or skipping instead of erroring, would break or silently gut valid backup restores.

O6_input_shapes: volume_snapshots containing a null element (snap == nil)
